checks_performed.detail: All agents have isolated inputs/, outputs/, results/ directories. 38 .isolation_marker files confirmed on disk.
create_input_manifest() generates per-agent ACL with allowed_read_paths (allowlist), allowed_write_paths, and restricted_paths (denylist). Manifest tracks isolation boundary, timestamp, and task.

check_access() implements multi-layered enforcement: allowlist -> denylist -> own directories -> default deny. Path resolution via Path.resolve() normalizes symlinks. Blocked access logged at WARNING level.
.isolation_marker files written to every agent directory at creation time. Content identifies agent-ID and role (input/output/result).

accept_result() copies outputs -> results (orchestrator-only). reject_result() writes structured rejection reports to rejected/ subfolder. get_all_accepted_results() only reads from results/ directories.
verify_isolation() tests orchestrator-level access (always passes) but does NOT simulate agent-level check_access() calls. Cannot prove agent-1 is blocked from agent-2's files via self-test.

isolation_strength: Strong - directory separation + manifest ACL + runtime enforcement (3 defense layers)

findings.finding: verify_isolation() does not test agent-to-agent isolation — only verifies orchestrator can read boundary markers. Should simulate agent-level check_access() calls.
findings.recommendation: Add cross-agent check_access() probes inside verify_isolation() to prove restricted_paths enforcement works.

findings.finding: _get_restricted_paths() inconsistent: blocks full directories for outputs/ and results/, but only manifest.json for inputs/.
findings.recommendation: Block full inputs/agent-{i} path for all i != agent_id for consistency.

findings.finding: String prefix matching in check_access() could potentially match unintended paths if naming conventions were subverted.
findings.recommendation: Consider using Path.relative_to() containment checks instead of str.startswith() for more precise boundary matching.

findings.finding: reject_result() writes rejection report but leaves original output file in place. Rejected outputs remain readable.
findings.recommendation: Consider moving rejected files to a quarantine directory to avoid confusion between accepted and rejected outputs.

findings.finding: allowed_write_paths includes agent's input directory (same dir as manifest.json), enabling potential manifest tampering if agent has direct filesystem access.
findings.recommendation: Remove str(agent_input_dir) from allowed_write_paths, or add manifest.json to restricted_paths for write operations.

security_assessment.notes: Isolation is enforced at application level only. No OS-level chmod/chown applied. No encryption. Agents with direct filesystem access could bypass isolation — but this requires subverting the subagent execution model first.
